title: Denver Omelette
subtitle: An American diner omelette with ham, pepper, and onion
excerpt: Beaten eggs cooked in butter until barely set, folded over a filling of diced ham, green pepper, and onion. The American diner answer to a simple, filling breakfast.
sourceNotes: Classic American diner omelette, also known as a Western omelette, adapted from standard short-order cooking.

content.text: The Denver omelette is a diner staple built around diced ham, green pepper, and onion, all folded inside a soft, barely-set egg. Work quickly once the eggs hit the pan. An overcooked omelette turns rubbery in seconds.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and pepper, and beat lightly with a fork until the yolks and whites just combine. Do not overbeat.

Melt half the butter in the larger frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and green pepper and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until softened. Add the ham and cook for 1 more minute. Tip onto a plate and keep warm.
For the first omelette, melt half the remaining butter in the omelette pan over a medium-high heat until it foams and begins to subside.
Pour in half the egg mixture. As the edges begin to set, use a spatula to draw them toward the centre, tilting the pan to let liquid egg run to the sides. Do this three or four times.
When the egg is just set on top with a little shine still visible, spoon half the ham and pepper filling across the centre. Scatter cheese over if using.
Fold the omelette in half or in thirds and slide onto a warm plate. Cook the second omelette in the same way.

items.symptom: The omelette is rubbery and overcooked.
items.cause: The heat was too high or it was left in the pan too long.
items.fix: Pull the pan from the heat while the top still looks slightly wet. The residual heat in the pan and the folding will finish the cooking.

items.cause: Too much filling was added or it was placed too close to the edge.
items.fix: Keep the filling confined to the centre third of the omelette, and use only enough to cover that area loosely.

items.cause: The egg set too firmly before folding, or the pan was dry.
items.fix: Use enough butter, keep the heat at medium-high rather than high, and fold while there is still a little shine left on top.
